name: Text input
purpose: Ask for one line of text, such as a name, an email address, or a link.
description: A labelled single-line field with an optional icon, a hint under it, and an error that is read with the field.

guidance.summary: Collects one line of free text that a person types, such as a name, an email address, or a link.
useWhen: The answer is short and open: a name, a title, an email address, a link, or a phone number.
It sits in a form, with its label above it, and is sent when the form is submitted.

avoidWhen.text: There are two to seven options a person should see at once.
The answer is one of a long, known list of options.
The answer runs to several sentences.
The text is a password or another secret.
The value is a small number a person nudges up or down.

states.label: Empty
states.description: Shows its label and, when it helps, an example as a placeholder.

states.label: Focus
states.description: A focus ring shows where typing goes.
states.how: Tab to the field, or click it.

states.label: Filled
states.description: Holds what the person typed, or the value the form started with.

states.label: With a hint
states.description: Help stays under the field, such as a format or why it is asked, and is read with it.

states.label: Invalid
states.description: The value cannot be used: the field is outlined, and the error under it says how to fix it.
states.how: error, set by the host after checking the value

states.label: Required
states.description: The form cannot be sent until the field is filled; the browser names the field that is missing.

dos.text: Keep a visible label above every field.
dos.why: A placeholder disappears as soon as people type, and with it what the field asked for.

dos.text: Choose the matching type: email, url, tel, or search.
dos.why: Phones show the right keyboard, and browsers can fill the value in.

dos.text: Write the error next to the field, saying how to fix the value.
dos.why: “Invalid input” tells people something is wrong but not what to do about it.

dos.text: Ask only for what you need, and mark it required.
dos.why: Every extra field is one more reason to abandon the form.

donts.text: Don’t use the placeholder as the label.
donts.why: It vanishes while typing, is often too faint to read, and is not reliably announced.

donts.text: Don’t show an error while the person is still typing.
donts.why: It scolds people for something they were about to fix. Check when they leave the field or submit.

donts.text: Don’t rely on red alone to show an error.
donts.why: About one man in twelve cannot tell red from green; the words carry the meaning.

donts.text: Don’t ask for the same information twice, such as confirming an email address.
donts.why: It doubles the work and the chances of a typo; show what they typed instead.

content: Labels are short nouns in sentence case: Work email, not Please enter your email.
Placeholders are examples, not instructions: name@company.com.
Errors say what to do: Enter an email address with an @, such as name@company.com.

keyboard.action: Submits the form the field belongs to.

notes: The label names the field; the hint and the error are tied to it with aria-describedby, so they are read with it.
An error sets aria-invalid, so assistive technology reports the field as invalid.
Set autocomplete to email, url, or tel so browsers and password managers can fill the value; a field rendered from Screen IR sets it from its type.

label.description: What the field asks for. It names the control and, with no name prop, the key its value is sent under.

name.description: The key the value is sent under, such as "email". Left out, it is the label in camelCase: "Work email" is sent as workEmail.

type.description: What kind of text: an email or a link gets the matching keyboard and autofill.

placeholder.description: An example of an answer, shown until a person types. It never replaces the label.

icon.description: Icon at the start of the field, such as "mail" or "search".

required.description: The form cannot be sent until a person fills this in.

hint.description: Help that stays under the field and is read with it, such as a format or a limit.

error.description: A problem with the value, shown under the field and announced with it. It marks the field invalid.
